audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[0].side and phases[1].side read "Skill" while content win[0] and win[1] read "Lux" — two answers to the same question. Separately, phases[4].side already read Lissandra but the why under it ("Final Spark online — anything the root catches dies to the laser math") described Lux winning level 6.
audit.why: Lux's Q reaches 1175 and E 1100 against Ice Shard's 725 and Ring of Frost's 450, so levels 1-2 are hers. At 6 Frozen Tomb is a 550-range point-blank stun that Lissandra sets up with Glacial Path, which beats an immobile Lux — that is why the side reads Lissandra and the why had to be rewritten to agree.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side and phases[1].side moved to Lux (win[0]/win[1] already read Lux, so no content edit). phases[4].why rewritten to describe Lissandra's level 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was described only as a lane flip; the actual numbers behind it — Frozen Tomb 120s at rank 1 from 550 range, Glacial Path 24s at rank 1 — were nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Her level 6 threat is entirely gated on a 120-second ultimate and a 24-second dash; without those numbers the advice to 'respect her ult' has no timer attached.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, phases[4].why, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent: Frozen Tomb cast on herself makes Lissandra untargetable and invulnerable, so a committed Final Spark or Q-E burst is wasted into it; and it heals her, so chip damage does not accumulate the way the poke plan assumes. breakdown.cooldowns also held no digit at all.
audit.why: Both are in Riot's own R text (untargetable, invulnerable, healing) and both are flagged in missingInteractions. They change when Lux may commit and whether she needs Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: Untargetability written into dontsFull[2].d; the anti-heal requirement written into breakdown.feeding (Morellonomicon named explicitly rather than a placeholder). breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt on real per-rank numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim under "Weave the passive auto after each spell"; dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim under "Burn R on waves while fights spawn".
audit.why: Both lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED — the title promises one thing and the body explains another.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to answer their own titles from this matchup's kit.

edits.before: Final Spark online — anything the root catches dies to the laser math. The lane becomes a geometry quiz.
edits.after: Frozen Tomb at 6 stuns from 550 and follows Ring of Frost — her lockdown beats your immobile frame.

edits.before: - Lissandra Glacial Path (Claw): matchup-defining — Her engage and escape in one button — she is immobile while it is down. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Prismatic Barrier has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Glacial Path (E): 24s at rank 1, 12s at rank 5 — her engage and escape in one button, and she is immobile while it is down. - Ring of Frost roots on 10s at rank 1 from 450. - Frozen Tomb is 120s at rank 1. - Your W Prismatic Barrier has one job: the moment it all goes wrong.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Illumination detonates on your next auto, so step in after E, auto once, and step out — chip she cannot answer inside her 725 Q.

edits.before: Lissandra whiffs Glacial Path (Claw) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Glacial Path is down 24 seconds at rank 1 — whiffed, the lane is yours.

edits.before: That is Lissandra’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: She sidesteps a raw Q at 1175; land E first, then bind the slow.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Frozen Tomb is 120s at rank 1 and she can cast it on herself to go untargetable — hold Final Spark until that window is spent.

edits.before: Lissandra wins by landing Glacial Path (Claw), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Lissandra wins by landing Ring of Frost into Frozen Tomb, chaining root to stun so you never get a step back out.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by outranging Frozen Tomb: it needs 550 units, so hold Q to peel her Glacial Path entry and laser from behind your front line.

edits.before: If Lissandra opens the score, reset expectations and respect Glacial Path (Claw) doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with E clears and stay relevant through root picks.
edits.after: If Lissandra opens the score, buy Morellonomicon early — Frozen Tomb heals her through your chip — and farm with E clears, staying relevant through root picks instead of solo redemption.

notes: phases[0]/[1] side moved to Lux with no paired win[N] edit because win[0] and win[1] already read Lux; a no-op edit would have been rejected and taken the chart group with it. phases[4] was the reverse defect — side already correct, why arguing with it — so only the why moved. Ratings left untouched throughout: the packet gives no basis for re-scoring and I did not want to move a number I could not ground. focus.text keeps "Glacial Path (Claw)": "claw" comes straight out of Riot's E text, so it reads as the AbilityName (Effect) convention rather than a fabrication.
